lines.text: 39 years ago today, the Dow fell 22.6%.
lines.say: Thirty-nine years ago today, the Dow fell twenty-two point six percent.

lines.text: In one day. From Friday's close, that'd be about 11,750 Dow points.
lines.say: In one day. From Friday's close, that'd be about eleven thousand seven hundred fifty Dow points.

lines.text: Its August record was 2,722. Black Monday left it at 1,739.
lines.say: Its August record was twenty-seven twenty-two. Black Monday left it at seventeen thirty-nine.

lines.text: It won those losses back by January 1989, then hit a new record that August.
lines.say: It won those losses back by January nineteen eighty-nine, then hit a new record that August.

lines.text: Early today, CNBC said Nasdaq futures rose after a rough week.
lines.say: Early today, CNBC said Nasdaq futures rose after a rough week.

lines.text: Last week the Nasdaq lost 4.5%, per the AP. The 1987 Dow lost five times that in a day.
lines.say: Last week the Nasdaq lost four and a half percent, per the A P. The nineteen eighty-seven Dow lost five times that in a day.

lines.text: After the crash came circuit breakers. Today, an S&P drop of 7% or 13% pauses trading, and 20% ends the day.
lines.say: After the crash came circuit breakers. Today, an S and P drop of seven or thirteen percent pauses trading, and twenty percent ends the day.

lines.text: So the Dow's worst percentage day took 22 months to reach a new high.
lines.say: So the Dow's worst percentage day took twenty-two months to reach a new high.

post.title: 39 years ago today, the Dow fell 22.6% in one day
post.ig:
39 years ago today, the Dow fell 22.6% in one day.
On October 19, 1987, the Dow dropped 508 points to 1,738.74. The same 22.6% from Friday's close of 52,002 would be about 11,750 points.
It regained the crash-day losses by January 1989 and set a new record in August 1989.
Today, S&P 500 circuit breakers pause trading for 15 minutes at -7% and -13% (before 3:25 p.m. ET) and stop it for the day at -20%. Nasdaq and S&P 500 futures rose early Monday after the Nasdaq's 4.5% weekly drop.
Sources: AP, CNBC, SEC/Investor.gov, CNN Money.
